target: PDT-II targets (1),(2),(4): test whether minimum-cost refinement path independence selects quadratic/Euclidean geometry.

infimal_pushforward_functoriality.statement: For arbitrary extended-real cost C and composable maps q1,q2, infimal pushforward satisfies q2_*(q1_*C)=(q2∘q1)_*C.
infimal_pushforward_functoriality.proof: Both sides equal inf{C(x): q2(q1(x))=z}; partitioning the feasible x by y=q1(x) does not alter the infimum.

quadratic_selection_from_path_independen.statement: Minimum-cost quotient path independence does not imply quadratic/Hilbert geometry.

n3_selection_from_refinement_associativi.statement: Refinement associativity/path independence alone cannot select n=3, because the same law holds in every tested dimension and for arbitrary sets/costs.

pdt_native_minimum_cost_rule.statement: PDT still must derive why coarse operational cost is the infimum over finer representatives. Even if derived, extra physical structure is required to select p=2/Hilbert geometry or n=3.

prior_art_boundary: Quotient norms use an infimum over representatives; iterated-infimum functoriality is elementary/standard. The Jordan-von Neumann parallelogram characterization of inner-product norms is classical. No novelty claim.
pdt_consequence: Cycle 104 quadratic transport is a special case of a much broader infimal pushforward law. Resource path independence cannot derive Euclidean geometry, composition associativity, or n=3.
next_kill_tests: Search PDT primitives for an independent parallelogram/polarization/operational-interference identity; do not infer it from quotient functoriality.
Test whether a PDT-native three-history cost identity excludes l1/lp and octonionic alternatives without assuming associativity.
